I implemented the lead's design note in `src/gov/guard/reads.py` only, added builder tests and wrote the CIT-E in W2-58's form. How each part of the note was met:
  1. Trees: `_trees` takes the session root plus the trees named by `git worktree list --porcelain -z`, run through the existing `_git`, each by real path. A project with no `.git` has only its own root. A worktree whose folder is missing is still refused by glob and has nothing to walk. A listing that fails or times out refuses with "the repository's worktrees cannot be listed".
  2. Run clones: a new `_Runs` part matches the hidden globs relative to any folder below the runs root, at any depth. The runs root is taken both as named and by real path, and is listed once per call; if it cannot be read, every call is refused with "the runs root cannot be read".
  3. Session in a run clone: its trees are the clone's own trees, the runs root, and the repository's trees found through the own folder's marker. The marker must be a regular file opened without following links and must name a git directory. Any failure refuses with "the repository's trees cannot be found from this run clone".
  4. The part: there is one hidden part per tree with the same globs and the same `HIDDEN_REFUSAL`, plus the runs-root part.
     - A tree is walked only when a search or listing starts at, in or above it.
     - The runs root is walked below the start (whole when the start is above it), never into `.git`, and is bounded.
     - Any folder that cannot be stat'ed or walked, other than one that is absent, refuses ("a hidden part's folder cannot be walked"). The (c) parts keep today's walk.
     - A listing fed at run time is refused when any tree holds a hidden file or the runs root holds any entry.
  5. Git routes:
     - `<rev>:<path>` in `git show` and `git cat-file`: refused whenever the path names a hidden path, whatever the tree.
     - `git -C <tree>`: the command is judged against that tree's part.
     - Patch routes (show, log -p, whatchanged -p, diff in its forms, format-patch, and `git show :/<text>`): when their pathspecs cover the hidden part, the guard asks git in a fixed form. First a `rev-parse` checks that every revision is a commit, because `git log` silently skips a blob. Then `log` or `diff` runs with `--no-ext-diff --no-textconv --name-only --no-renames --diff-merges=separate --full-history`, the side-choosing options, `--end-of-options`, the revisions and `:(top,glob)` pathspecs. The `-C`, `--git-dir` and `--work-tree` the command gives are passed on.
     - `git grep <rev>`, `git grep --cached` and `git archive <rev>`: checked with `ls-tree -r --full-tree` or `ls-files --cached`.
     - Any git answer that cannot be had refuses with "git cannot say whether a revision holds the hidden part". `git worktree list` stays allowed.
  6. Cost: an unmeasured session never reaches any new code (no new git call; a builder test shows zero `_git` calls). A measured session lists its trees once per call, shared between the session role and the subagent role (a builder test shows exactly one `worktree list`).
  7. Unchanged: (a), (b) and (c); the visible parts; which sessions are measured; `check_sets`; `_git`'s environment; every message except the five new causes.
  8. Residuals R1–R6 are recorded in CIT-E §5, plus the over-refusals this change accepts on the fail-closed side.
